chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:

There is no fasting person who is present with a people who are eating except that his limbs glorify [Allah], and the angels send blessings upon him, and their blessings are a seeking of forgiveness for him.

key_terms.استغفار: Seeking forgiveness (istighfar) - the angels' blessings take the form of asking God to forgive the fasting person
key_terms.سبحت أعضاؤه: His limbs glorify - a metaphor for the entire body participating in worship through fasting
key_terms.صائم: Fasting person - one who abstains from food and drink for the sake of God

ai.seo_question: What happens to a fasting person who is present while others eat in Islam?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW), narrated through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his forefathers, describes the spiritual reward of a fasting person who exercises patience while others eat around him. His very limbs glorify God, and the angels pray for his forgiveness. This teaching, delivered at the Eighty-Sixth Assembly in Rajab 368 AH, emphasizes that true patience during fasting -- especially when witnessing others eat -- draws angelic intercession and divine mercy.
